own_solution.law: The acoustic impedances are Z1 = rho1*c1 = 411.6 Pa s/m and Z2 = rho2*c2 = 1479036 Pa s/m. Pressure and normal-velocity continuity give pt = [2Z2/(Z1+Z2)]sqrt(2Z1*Ii). Equivalently, It = [4Z1Z2/(Z1+Z2)^2]Ii and pt = sqrt(2Z2*It).
assumptions: Use small-amplitude plane-wave acoustics with the stated uniform, lossless fluids and interface conditions.
Pressure amplitude denotes peak amplitude and intensity denotes time-averaged intensity.
The requested measurement concerns the steady wave at the current incident intensity; an earlier trial is separate.

notes: All certified numerical answers agree with the acoustic transmission relations. Increasing the current incident intensity by 0.003, 0.006 or 0.009 W/m² gives respectively 7.02599, 7.69659 or 8.31326 Pa. The second source has no path to the water, and a change on an earlier trial does not alter the stated current-trial intensity. Frequency cancels because Z = rho*(c/f)*f = rho*c; the supplied cancellation expressions correctly reproduce the transmission calculation at all listed positive frequencies.
